Not re-run (settled). One meta-check I did do: `recipeGuards.test.ts` imports `{ components } from './index'` and iterates `Object.entries(components)` with no allowlist — confirmed the two new recipes (`ZimmColourSwatch`, `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`) are genuinely walked by the "hard styling gate," not skipped by omission. Clean.

## Angle 2 — Tokens

Semantic-intent check on every `var(--zimm-color-*)` in the new files:

- `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:31` `backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-bg-02)'` — background category on a `background` prop. Match.
- `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:40` `borderBottomColor: 'var(--zimm-color-border-focus)'` — border category on a `border-color` prop. Match.
- `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:193` and `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts:97` `color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)'` — text category on `color`. Match.
- `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts:167` `color: 'var(--zimm-color-icon-disabled)'` — icon category on `color`, applied to the button that wraps a `ZimmIcon` (which resolves `color="currentColor"` and inherits it). Match.

No mismatches found. Clean — this angle earns its keep and is genuinely clear, not vacuous.

## Angle 3 — Styling conformance

No bare Chakra token keys, no raw hex/px literals, no array-shorthand responsive steps, both recipes correctly namespaced and registered in `theme/components/index.ts:17-18,40-41`. Clean on the mechanical checks.

**Recipe state exhaustiveness — 🔴 must-fix, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM.**
Neither new interactive recipe part defines `_hover`:
```
grep -n "_hover" zimmColourSwatch.css.ts zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts   → no matches
```
Both `swatch` (`zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:18-82`, `cursor: 'pointer'`, a real `<a>`/anchor when `href` is set) and `pageButton` (`zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts:147-175`, a real `<button>`) have `_focusVisible` (and `pageButton` has `_disabled`), but zero mouse-hover feedback. This isn't a hypothetical — I checked every other interactive recipe in `ui-kits/`: `zimmNavItem.css.ts`, `zimmTextInput.css.ts`, and `zimmButton.css.ts` **all** define `_hover`. The swatch recipe's own comment (`zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:47`) explicitly says it "mirrors `zimmNavItem.css.ts`'s own focus-ring block" — but didn't carry over that same file's hover block. Base SFCC's own `swatch-group.js` theme (the file colour swatches used *before* this PR) also defines `_hover` for both its `circle` and `square` variants. So: two independent same-codebase precedents and the inherited base behaviour all have hover feedback; the two new controls have none, and no gate catches it. I could not check Figma directly (no MCP tool in my toolset for this session — see "What I could not verify"), so I can't confirm whether a dedicated Hover node exists, but the codebase-convention violation stands on its own regardless of that answer.

**Stale comment — 🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF** (this is the item flagged for a second look).
`zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts:159-168`: the comment says "only the cursor affordance is set here, which is a UX keyword, not a design token," but the `_disabled` block right below sets both `cursor: 'not-allowed'` (line 166) **and** `color: 'var(--zimm-color-icon-disabled)'` (line 167). I confirmed via `git log`/`git blame` reasoning (commit `0aff491` "post-build fixes... disabled chevron colour") that the colour line was added after the comment was written and the comment was never updated. The code is correct — `--zimm-color-icon-disabled` is a real, Figma-sourced token, and it correctly cascades to the `ZimmIcon` inside via `currentColor` (verified: `ZimmIcon` defaults `color="currentColor"` and the pagination buttons pass no explicit `color` override, so the parent's disabled `color` does reach the chevron glyph). Only the comment is wrong.

## Angle 4 — Structure

Named exports match folder names, props types follow `<Component>Props`, both new components have stories and test files. Neither `ZimmColourSwatchProps` nor `ZimmColourSwatchGroupProps` is exported — consumed instead via `React.ComponentProps<typeof X>` in tests/stories — I checked every sibling `ui-kits` component (`zimmProductMeta`, `zimmProductPrice`, `zimmProductStyleCode`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmInputAction`, `zimmSubscribeSection`) and **none** of them extract a `types.ts` file either, even though their types are consumed by the exact same story/test siblings — so this is consistent with real, established codebase precedent, not a deviation from `components.md`'s letter-of-the-law reading. Clean.

**Missing test file — 🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF.**
`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` has no `index.test.ts(x)` in either base or head (`find` confirms only `index.tsx` exists in that folder). This file gained real new branching logic in this PR: the `renderHeader ?? <ProductViewHeader>` default, and `renderVariationAttribute?.(attr) ?? renderDefaultVariationAttribute(attr)` (line 865). Per `testing.md`, "a component with real logic (branching, prop→JSX mapping decisions) gets its own test file... even when the state it renders is owned by a hook that already has its own test." The base template itself ships `product-view/index.test.js` for comparison, so there's an existing precedent this override doesn't follow. This logic is currently only exercised indirectly (through `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s own tests proving *its* contract, and Storybook), never proving `ProductView`'s own fallback-wiring contract from its own folder.

## Angle 5 — Imports

Clean. No base-path import of an already-overridden component (`product-view/index.tsx` imports nothing from `ui-kits/`; `product-detail/index.tsx:75` imports `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` via a 2-level relative path); no circular imports (`zimmColourSwatch` doesn't import `zimmColourSwatchGroup`); no `../../../..` chains beyond 2 levels; no later-sprint feature imports.

## Angle 6 — Accessibility

No `<img>` tags (swatch fill is a CSS `background-image`, consistent with base SFCC's own pattern). Pagination buttons carry `aria-label` (`index.tsx:206,215`). No non-native element has an `onClick` without accompanying semantics — the href-absent `chakra.span` branch has **no** `onClick` at all, so the role/tabIndex/onKeyDown rule doesn't trigger (confirmed this branch is currently unreachable from any live caller — `product-detail/index.tsx` never invokes `controlledVariationValues` mode, and I traced the real base hook (`use-variation-attributes.js:152-153`) to confirm `href: null` only occurs in that mode).

I independently verified the CodeRabbit-flagged, "not fully merge-ready" WCAG 2.1.1 blocker ("keyboard users may be unable to enter the swatch control" when paginated away from the selection) is genuinely fixed in `54e924f` — not just by reading the diff, but by writing and running a real fixture against the live component (see React logic correctness below). Confirmed fixed. CodeRabbit's own thread shows the same conclusion and resolved the thread.

## Angle 7 — Against the ticket

All four formal ACs plus the Figma pagination annotation are satisfied by the code as written — traced each one directly:
- AC1 (single colour → text only): `populated.length > 1` gate, `index.tsx:223`.
- AC2 (index image as swatch): `imageUrl` → `background-image`, resolved at the page level from `disBaseLink || link` (`product-detail/index.tsx:923`), matches base's own fallback order.
- AC3 (selected indication): `isSelected` → `aria-checked` + bottom-border recipe branch.
- AC4 (URL update, no reload): `ColourSwatchLink = chakra(RouteLink)`, same primitive base SFCC's own `Swatch` uses.
- AC5 (unpopulated filtered): `populated = values.filter(v => Boolean(v.imageUrl))`, proven not to key on any other field by its own test.
- Pagination (>4 → chevrons, truncation): `isPaginated`/`SWATCHES_PER_PAGE`/`labelName` truncation triad — all present.

**Silent loss of unavailable-colour treatment — 🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, risk of recurring (UNIFORM-risk).**
Not a violation of any of the four stated ACs (none of them mention stock state), but a real, undocumented behavioural narrowing: `grep -n "orderable" overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` returns nothing — `v.orderable` is never forwarded into `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`, and `ZimmColourSwatchValue` has no such field at all. Before this PR, a colour attribute rendered through the same `Swatch`/`SwatchGroup` path as size, which gives an unorderable value a diagonal-strikethrough visual (`node_modules/.../theme/components/project/swatch-group.js:56,83-91`, `props.disabled` branch) — cosmetic only (it never blocked the click/navigation in base either, so this is not a functional/navigation regression), but real. After this PR, every populated colour renders identically regardless of stock, with zero comment anywhere acknowledging the trade-off (contrast with the pagination `_disabled` block, which *does* have an explicit "no confirmed Figma spec" comment for its own gap). Worth a design confirmation before treating this as accepted scope.

## Angle 8 — Intra-step DRY

`SWATCHES_PER_PAGE` is correctly centralised in `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts` and imported (never re-typed) by `index.tsx`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`, and `index.test.tsx` — confirmed via grep, no duplicate literal `4` used for page size anywhere. `GROUP_LABEL_MESSAGE`'s reuse of base SFCC's own `swatch_group.selected.label` id is accurate (confirmed the id exists verbatim in `node_modules/.../swatch-group/index.jsx`). Clean.

**🔵 note, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM (2 files).** `href?: string` is declared identically in `zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:25` and `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:45`, but the real SFCC hook this data ultimately comes from returns `href: null` (not `undefined`) in controlled mode — confirmed at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variation-attributes.js:152-153`. The component's own doc comment even names this ("SFCC's own `useVariationAttributes` returns `href: null`"), so the type should be `string | null` to match what its own documentation says can arrive. No functional bug (`if (href)` treats both falsy values identically), purely a type-accuracy gap in two co-located places.

## Correctness/regression (`??` fallback + wiring)

Verified clean. `renderVariationAttribute?.(attr) ?? renderDefaultVariationAttribute(attr)` (`product-view/index.tsx:865`): both `null` and `undefined` returned by the override fall through to base rendering — matches the final, corrected doc comment (`index.tsx:188-190`, fixed by commit `2d8a9a7`) exactly. `product-detail/index.tsx:914-926` restricts to `attr.id === COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID` only, returning `undefined` for every other attribute (size), correctly falling through to base rendering for those. Set/bundle `ProductView` instances (`product-detail/index.tsx:811-827`, `837-887`) pass neither `renderHeader` nor `renderVariationAttribute` — confirmed untouched, as claimed.

## Conventions/tier ownership

No undisclosed protected path touched — full file list cross-checked against `frozenFiles.md`/`protectedFiles.md`; only the disclosed Tier 1 (`colour.ts`, `zimmTokens.ts`) and Tier 2 (`theme/components/index.ts`) paths are in scope, both already flagged in the PR body and by the repo's own `protected-file-guard` bot.

**🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM (will recur every regen).** `.claude/registry/*.md` is genuinely regenerated output (not hand-edited — confirmed via the CodeRabbit thread, where `generateRegistry.mjs` is cited as the source and a direct-edit attempt was correctly declined), but the generator itself is non-deterministic/inaccurate: 33 lines in `components.md` and ~14 in `hooks.md` changed for components/hooks this PR never touches (`App`, `Field`, `Link`, `Register`, `Search`, `useCurrentBasket`, `useMultiSite`, etc. — consumer counts shifting by ±1 to ±11 with no plausible causal link to colour swatches). Two entries got **factually wrong** descriptions: `ShopperAgent`'s changed from "Main ShopperAgent component that initializes and manages the embedded messaging service..." to "Validates that a URL is from a trusted Salesforce domain" (`components.md`), and `useMiaw`'s changed from "Custom hook that initializes embedded messaging when the script is loaded" to "Maps BCP-47 locales to Salesforce language codes" (`hooks.md`) — neither file was touched by this PR, and neither description matches the hook/component it's attached to. This is a generator defect surfaced by, not caused by, this PR, but it means every future PR's registry diff will bury real changes in unrelated noise, and the registry's own descriptions are actively wrong for at least these two entries as of this commit.

## Contract fidelity

Clean. Grepped both new files for any SFCC-shape leakage (`Sfcc`, `ShopperProductsTypes`, `disBaseLink`, `commerce-sdk`) — zero matches. Import lists are React/Chakra/react-router-dom/react-intl/sibling-atoms only. All SFCC-shape resolution (`disBaseLink || link`, `v.href`) happens at the page level (`product-detail/index.tsx`), exactly as claimed.

## Test coverage quality

`ZimmColourSwatch`/`ZimmColourSwatchGroup` test files are genuinely good: they assert on rendered output (roles, `aria-checked`, computed styles) rather than implementation, and include real regression tests for two previously-fixed bugs (the z-index/stacking focus-ring fix, the fixed-width-footprint layout fix). `product-view/index.tsx`'s missing test file is covered above (Angle 4).

**🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF.** No test — Vitest or Storybook `play` — exercises the *actual runtime transition* the CodeRabbit WCAG blocker and the "dead first click" fix were about. Every existing pagination test either (a) checks a fresh mount already on the correct/incorrect page (`index.test.tsx:134-168`), or (b) clicks "Next"/"Previous" but only asserts on `width` (`index.test.tsx:170-217`) or item count (`index.stories.tsx:165-196`), never on `tabindex`/`aria-checked` post-click. I confirmed the logic is actually correct by writing and running two throwaway probes directly against the component (see next section) — but that proof lives in my scratch work, not in the shipped suite. If a future refactor reintroduces the raw-`pageStart` functional-updater pattern CodeRabbit flagged, nothing in this PR's own test suite would catch it.

## React logic correctness

This step introduces real stateful logic (`useState(selectedPageStart)` seeded from a prop-derived value, a `useEffect` resync, and pagination handlers that were the subject of a specific stale-state bug fix), so I wrote fixtures rather than just reading the diff.

**Falsification attempt — PASSED (i.e., code is correct), CONFIRMED by execution, not just reasoning.** I wrote a temporary test file (`__auditProbe__.test.tsx`, deleted immediately after, `git status` confirmed clean) with two cases against the real, unmodified component:
1. Navigate to page 3 of 12 items, shrink to 7 items while mounted (stale raw `pageStart=8` vs. new `lastPageStart=4`), then fire a **single** click of "Previous colours." If the handlers still read raw `pageStart` via a functional updater (the pre-fix shape CodeRabbit flagged at `index.tsx:149`), this would be the exact "dead first click" — the click computes off the stale value and produces no visible change. Result: **one click correctly moved from items 4-6 to items 0-3.** The fix (reading `currentPageStart`, the clamped derived value, per commit `54e924f`) holds.
2. Mount with `selectedValue="C0"` (page 1), then re-render with `selectedValue="C7"` (a different page) with **no click at all** — the "prop that seeds state on mount receives a different value on a re-render" case. Result: the `useEffect` on `selectedPageStart` correctly moved the window and correctly recomputed which single swatch carries `tabindex="0"`.

Both passed on the first run against the actual PR code. This independently corroborates CodeRabbit's own resolution of both threads.

**🔵 note, PLAUSIBLE (reasoned, not reproduced).** Because `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` has no product-identity `key` anywhere up its tree (`attr.id` is always the literal string `'color'`), the same component instance persists across a full product-to-product navigation (React Router keeps `ProductDetail` mounted across `:productId` changes). If a shopper navigates from a paginated product sitting on page N to a *different*, also-paginated product whose `lastPageStart` happens to still be ≥ the stale raw `pageStart`, the render clamp (`currentPageStart = Math.min(pageStart, lastPageStart)`) can pass through a stale, wrong page for one paint before the `useEffect` corrects it on the next tick. This is a single-frame flash at worst (final state is always correct — confirmed by probe 2 above), not a functional break, and I could not construct a deterministic repro for it: jsdom/testing-library flush effects synchronously within `render`/`rerender`, so there is no way to observe an intermediate "pre-effect" frame in this test environment — which is itself consistent with this being a real-browser-paint-timing-only edge case that no unit test in this codebase's stack could ever directly catch either way.

Both are inherited, not introduced. `aria-label={name}` is a plain React attribute (auto-escaped), no injection surface.

Everything the orchestrator already Figma-verified (dimensions, aspect ratio, background colour, selected border colour, focus-ring offset/colour, `caption` textStyle, label-row layout, `icon.disabled` token) is not repeated here. This table covers only what's newly open from my pass:

This step introduces real stateful logic (`useState(selectedPageStart)` seeded from a prop-derived value, a `useEffect` resync, and pagination handlers that were the subject of a specific stale-state bug fix), so I wrote fixtures rather than just reading the diff.

**Falsification attempt — PASSED (i.e., code is correct), CONFIRMED by execution, not just reasoning.** I wrote a temporary test file (`__auditProbe__.test.tsx`, deleted immediately after, `git status` confirmed clean) with two cases against the real, unmodified component:
1. Navigate to page 3 of 12 items, shrink to 7 items while mounted (stale raw `pageStart=8` vs. new `lastPageStart=4`), then fire a **single** click of "Previous colours." If the handlers still read raw `pageStart` via a functional updater (the pre-fix shape CodeRabbit flagged at `index.tsx:149`), this would be the exact "dead first click" — the click computes off the stale value and produces no visible change. Result: **one click correctly moved from items 4-6 to items 0-3.** The fix (reading `currentPageStart`, the clamped derived value, per commit `54e924f`) holds.
2. Mount with `selectedValue="C0"` (page 1), then re-render with `selectedValue="C7"` (a different page) with **no click at all** — the "prop that seeds state on mount receives a different value on a re-render" case. Result: the `useEffect` on `selectedPageStart` correctly moved the window and correctly recomputed which single swatch carries `tabindex="0"`.

Both passed on the first run against the actual PR code. This independently corroborates CodeRabbit's own resolution of both threads.

**🔵 note, PLAUSIBLE (reasoned, not reproduced).** Because `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` has no product-identity `key` anywhere up its tree (`attr.id` is always the literal string `'color'`), the same component instance persists across a full product-to-product navigation (React Router keeps `ProductDetail` mounted across `:productId` changes). You're in findings-verification mode, not scoring mode. Reviewing PR #74 on zimmermann-pwa (branch `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches`, base `269d5d40149b9947111dd87e78d37b92fccd4c99`, head `54e924ffddabef17aeabb983873c60855dd06aac` = current HEAD, no checkout needed — read the working tree as-is or `git diff` the range yourself).

For each finding below: does it survive scrutiny? Reproduce it from source or say you could not. Return CONFIRMED (reproduced from source), PLAUSIBLE (consistent with what you read, decisive evidence missing — say exactly what would settle it), or UNSUPPORTED (the citation doesn't support the claim — say what's actually true). Where a finding's conclusion is broader than its search supports, downgrade it and say so.

## Findings to verify

**F1 — Lint regression.** Claim: `npm run lint` on HEAD produces 2 more errors than on BASE, both prettier-formatting errors in PR-added files: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:86` and `.../zimmColourSwatch/index.test.tsx:119`. I measured this myself by running the gate on both SHAs (base=4 errors/16 warnings, head=6 errors/16 warnings, same 16 warnings just line-shifted). You can re-run `npm run lint` on HEAD only to confirm those 2 specific errors still exist at those locations — no need to reconstruct BASE.

**F2 — Stale/self-contradictory comment.** File `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`, around lines 159-168. Claim: the comment immediately above the `pageButton._disabled` object says "No confirmed Figma spec for a disabled visual treatment on this control... only the cursor affordance is set here, which is a UX keyword, not a design token" — but the `_disabled` object right below it sets BOTH `cursor: 'not-allowed'` AND `color: 'var(--zimm-color-icon-disabled)'`, which IS a real visual treatment via a real design token, directly contradicting the comment. Read the actual lines and confirm or refute.

**F3 — Over-delivery: unused `href`-absent branch.** Files `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx` (the `href?: string` prop and the `if (href) {...} return <chakra.span>...` branch) and `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx`. Claim: this PR's only real wiring (`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`, the `renderVariationAttribute` prop passed to the main uncontrolled `<ProductView>`) always supplies a real `href` for every colour value — `href: null`/undefined only occurs via SFCC's controlled-mode variation-attributes path (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variation-attributes.js`, the `isControlled`/`controlledVariationValues` branch), which this PR never wires `renderVariationAttribute` into (not `product-view-modal`, not `bonus-product-view-modal`). So the href-absent branch, its dedicated prop, several unit tests, and a whole Storybook story currently have no live caller anywhere in this PR's actual scope. Verify by tracing: does `product-detail/index.tsx` ever render `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`/pass `renderVariationAttribute` anywhere other than the one call site on the main product `<ProductView>`? Does that hook's controlled-mode branch really only trigger from a different component this PR doesn't touch?

**F4 — Missing `_hover` state, codebase-convention violation.** Files `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` and `.../zimmColourSwatchGroup/zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`. Claim: neither of this PR's two new interactive recipes (`swatch` part, an anchor/span; `pageButton` part, a button) defines a `_hover` block, while every other interactive recipe already in `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` — check `zimmNavItem/zimmNavItem.css.ts`, `zimmTextInput/zimmTextInput.css.ts`, `zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts` — does define one. I independently checked Figma myself (file `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`, node `40000307:13823` "pdp/product-colour-picker" and node `40003328:115591` "Pagination") and confirmed there is genuinely no Hover-state variant defined anywhere in this component set (only Unselected/Selected/Focus states exist) — so this is a codebase-convention question, not a missed Figma spec. Just verify the code-side claim: do the 3 cited sibling files really all define `_hover`, and do the 2 new files really define none?

**F5 — Missing test file for `product-view/index.tsx`.** Claim: `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` gained real new branching logic in this PR (the `renderVariationAttribute?.(attr) ?? renderDefaultVariationAttribute(attr)` fallback) but has no `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx` anywhere in its folder, on either base or head. Verify the file genuinely doesn't exist (not just "didn't show up in a grep").

**F6 — Silent loss of unorderable/out-of-stock colour treatment.** Claim: `v.orderable` (a real field on the SFCC variation value shape) is never forwarded from `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` into `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s `values` mapping, and `ZimmColourSwatchValue`'s type has no such field at all — so an unorderable-but-image-populated colour now renders identically to an orderable one, with no comment anywhere acknowledging this narrowing (contrast with the `pageButton._disabled` block, which does have an explicit comment about its own unspecified state). Verify: grep for `orderable` in `product-detail/index.tsx` and in the `zimmColourSwatchGroup`/`zimmColourSwatch` type definitions — is it really absent end to end?

**F7 — `href` type should include `null`.** Claim: `href?: string` is declared in both `zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx` and `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx`, but the real hook this data traces back to (`use-variation-attributes.js`) returns `href: null` (not `undefined`) in its controlled-mode branch — a type-accuracy gap, not a functional bug (`if (href)` treats both the same). Verify the hook really returns `null` specifically, not `undefined`, in that branch.

**F8 — Pagination test-suite doesn't test the actual click-triggered transition.** File `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.test.tsx`. Claim: existing tests either check a fresh mount already on the correct/wrong page, or click prev/next and assert only on rendered `width`/item-count — none clicks a pagination button and then asserts on `tabindex`/`aria-checked` of the resulting swatches. This means nothing in the shipped suite would catch a regression of the WCAG roving-tabindex-after-paging fix if it were reintroduced. Verify by reading the actual test file's assertions after each `userEvent.click` on a pagination button.

**F9 — Single-frame stale-pagination flash on cross-product navigation (already labeled PLAUSIBLE by its source, not CONFIRMED).** Claim: because no component in the tree keys `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`/`ProductView` by product identity, and `pageStart` state persists across a prop-driven re-render (only corrected by a `useEffect` on the next tick), navigating from one paginated product to a different paginated product could in principle paint one stale frame before self-correcting. The original source couldn't construct a jsdom repro (effects flush synchronously in RTL) and says so explicitly. Don't try to force a repro either — just assess whether the reasoning about the component tree (no remount, effect-based correction) holds up from reading the actual code, and state plainly that this remains unconfirmed by execution either way.

## What's already settled — don't re-litigate

- All 5 real Jira ACs (single-colour label-only, swatch-per-populated-colour, selected-indication, URL-update-without-reload, unpopulated-image-filtered) are independently confirmed implemented correctly by two separate passes already (file:line evidence exists) — not in question.
- Every colour/spacing/typography token match against live Figma (bottom-border colour/width, background colour, focus-ring colour/width/offset, `caption` textStyle, disabled-chevron colour) was verified directly against the Figma file by a human-directed pass, including live computed-style verification in a running Storybook via real keyboard `Tab` navigation. Not in question.
- The Tier 1 foundation-file edit (`colour.ts`/`zimmTokens.ts`) was independently re-verified as genuinely authorized (`gh api` confirms the PR author is both a `tier-1-approvers` member and repo admin) by two separate checks already. Not in question — don't re-check GitHub team membership.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` are clean/unchanged between base and head — not in question.
- `npm run test` (vitest) is 433/433 passing on head, no regressions — not in question.

Report back with each finding's ID, verdict (CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE/UNSUPPORTED), and one line of evidence or the specific gap in evidence.

All verification is back — every core finding from both audit passes holds up, with one appropriately downgraded to PLAUSIBLE where the original phrasing overstated the record. Here's the full picture.

## Gates — head vs. base, measured directly (not from CI)

| Gate | Base (`269d5d4`) | Head (`54e924f`) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | 0 errors | 0 errors | clean |
| `audit:tokens` | 4 unacknowledged violations | same 4, unchanged | no new violations — inherited debt |
| `npm run lint` | 4 errors / 16 warnings | **6 errors** / 16 warnings | **+2 new prettier errors, in this PR's own new files** |
| `npm run test` (vitest) | 408/408 passed (26 files) | 433/433 passed (28 files) | clean, no regressions |

CI's own rollup shows `Playwright E2E (localhost)` and `Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)` as **SKIPPED**, not passed — expected here, since AC4 has no `.feature` file yet (disclosed gap, consistent with the mandatory gherkin-first workflow), not a red flag being hidden by a green check.

## Findings, ranked by cost of ignoring them

1. **CONFIRMED — the two previously-blocking pagination bugs have no regression test for their actual trigger.** `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.test.tsx`. CodeRabbit's round-1 "Major" WCAG finding (keyboard users can get stranded when paged away from the selection) and the "dead first click" bug are both genuinely fixed — proven by direct execution against the real component, not just by reading the diff — but nothing in the *shipped* suite clicks a pagination button and then asserts on `tabindex`/`aria-checked` afterward. Existing tests either check a fresh mount already on the right page, or click and only check width/count. A future refactor could silently reintroduce either bug with zero red tests.

2. **CONFIRMED — both new interactive controls ship with no `_hover` state.** `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` (the swatch itself), `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts` (`pageButton`). Every other interactive recipe in `ui-kits/` — `zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput`, `zimmButton` — defines one. I checked Figma myself: there's no hover variant anywhere in this component's design either, so nothing was *missed* from spec — but it's a real break from this codebase's own habit of giving every interactive control some hover feedback even without one.

3. **Real, confirmed behaviour — softened from the original framing.** Unorderable/out-of-stock colours now render identically to available ones. `orderable` exists on the real SFCC data and drives a disabled/strikethrough treatment in base's own `Swatch`, but this PR's mapping (`product-detail/index.tsx`) never reads it, and `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s types have no such field. There *is* code commentary explaining why the AC5 filter keys on image-population rather than stock — so this isn't silent in the way I first flagged — but nothing addresses the specific consequence that a shopper can no longer tell an unorderable colour apart before clicking it.

4. **CONFIRMED — over-delivery: the "no href" / quick-view-modal branch has no live caller anywhere in this PR.** `zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx`'s `href?` prop and its inert-`<span>` branch, plus 5 of its 9 unit tests and a whole Storybook story. Traced end to end: this PR's one real wiring always supplies a real `href`; `href: null` only ever happens via a controlled-mode path (`product-view-modal`/`bonus-product-view-modal`) that isn't overridden anywhere in this repo and that this PR never touches.

5. **CONFIRMED — no test file for `product-view/index.tsx`'s new logic.** It gained real branching (`renderVariationAttribute?.(attr) ?? renderDefaultVariationAttribute(attr)`) but has never had a test file, on base or head, despite the upstream base template shipping one. The logic itself is simple and independently proven correct by direct execution — this is a coverage gap, not a live bug.

6. **Small, low-controversy cleanups** (all CONFIRMED, none need a judgment call):
   - `npm run lint` fails on head from 2 new prettier-formatting errors in this PR's own files (`zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:86`, `index.test.tsx:119`).
   - `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts:159-168`'s comment says "only the cursor affordance is set here... not a design token" directly above code that also sets a real colour token — stale, left over from before the disabled-chevron-colour fix landed in a later commit.
   - `href?: string` (two files) should be `href?: string | null` — the real SFCC hook returns `null`, not `undefined`, there. No functional impact.

7. **PLAUSIBLE, structurally reasoned, genuinely unconfirmable in this test stack.** No component between the route and `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` carries a product-identity `key`, and `pageStart` is corrected only by a `useEffect` (not `useLayoutEffect`). Navigating same-route from one paginated product to a differently-paginated one could in principle paint one stale frame before self-correcting. Final state is always right; this would need a real browser to ever settle, not a unit test.

**Out of scope — not this PR's problem:**
- `.claude/registry/components.md`/`hooks.md`'s generator script produces unrelated churn *and* two factually wrong descriptions (`ShopperAgent`, `useMiaw`) that predate this PR entirely. Real bug, pre-existing. I've spun this off as its own flag rather than raising it here.
- The `product-detail/` squad-ownership conflict (CODEOWNERS vs. both squad docs) — pre-existing, already disclosed in the PR and correctly declined in the CodeRabbit thread.

## Scope verdict

Delivers exactly SFCC-91's real scope — all 5 formal ACs plus the Figma-specified pagination behaviour — and correctly excludes the deferred style-code/full-reload AC now owned by SFCC-708. The Tier 1 foundation-file token addition is legitimate and disclosed; I independently re-confirmed your GitHub identity really is both a `tier-1-approvers` member and repo admin, so the self-authorization in the PR body checks out for real. Finding #4 above is the one contained over-delivery.

## What nobody verified

- Whether Figma defines any "unavailable but populated" colour-swatch treatment — finding #3 rests on code/precedent (base `Swatch`'s own disabled logic), not a confirmed absence from Figma.
- Finding #7 — would need real-browser E2E to ever settle.
- AC4's no-reload behaviour is verified at code/Storybook level (same `RouteLink` primitive as base) but not via an actual Playwright journey — expected, given no `.feature` file exists yet.
- The required non-author Tier 2 review on `theme/components/index.ts` hasn't happened — that's the actual merge gate, not something this review substitutes for.
- I only checked the desktop-default Storybook viewport, not mobile/responsive behaviour.

**One premise everything I ran converged on independently:** the href-absent branch is currently dead code in this PR's own wiring. Worth attacking directly if you think that's wrong.

I spun off the registry-generator bug as a separate flag since it's real but unrelated to this PR. Now, four things worth your actual call:

input.title: Fix generateRegistry.mjs producing wrong descriptions

content.text:
Got it — here's how that resolves things:

- **Hover state**: dropped, no PR action (you've confirmed it's out of spec/scope).
- **Stock-state signal**: dropped, no PR action — the swatch stays clickable and the Add-to-Bag button carries the disabled/unorderable signal once that colour's selected, so nothing's actually lost, it's just surfaced downstream rather than on the swatch itself.
- **Unused href branch**: kept as deliberate infra, no PR action.
- **Pagination test gap**: this is the one real ask.

That leaves one substantive comment plus the mechanical cleanups (lint, stale comment, href type) and the product-view test-file gap I hadn't asked about separately — including it here since it's the same "test the branching, not just the downstream state" logic as the pagination gap you just confirmed you want. Here's the full comment set I'd post:

**General comment:**
> Reviewed against SFCC-91's actual Jira ACs (the structured Acceptance Criteria field, not this PR's own paraphrase) and the live Figma file. All five ACs plus the Figma pagination annotation are implemented correctly, with exact fidelity on the design tokens — colour, spacing, and focus ring all measured as exact matches, including a live keyboard-driven check in Storybook. One thing worth landing before merge, four small cleanups, everything else accepted as out of this ticket's scope.

**Inline — `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.test.tsx:170-217`:**
> This test clicks the pagination buttons but only asserts on width/radio count afterward. This file is what guards the two round-1 fixes (the roving-tabindex-after-paging fix and the stale-`pageStart` dead-click fix) — worth adding an assertion that checks `tabindex`/`aria-checked` on the resulting swatches after the click, not just the state before mount. Right now a regression of either fix could land with this whole suite green.

**Inline — `zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:86` and `zimmColourSwatch/index.test.tsx:119`:**
> `npm run lint` fails on this branch from two new prettier-formatting errors here, neither present on develop. `npx prettier --write` on both should clear it.

**Inline — `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts:159-168`:**
> This comment says "only the cursor affordance is set here, which is a UX keyword, not a design token," but the block right below also sets `color: 'var(--zimm-color-icon-disabled)'`, a real token. Looks like the colour line landed in the later disabled-chevron-colour fix without this comment getting updated to match.

**Inline — `zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx` and `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` (`href?: string`):**
> The hook this traces back to (`use-variation-attributes.js`) returns `href: null`, not `undefined`, in its controlled-mode branch. `href?: string | null` would match what can actually arrive, per `typescript.md`'s typing guidance. No functional difference today since `if (href)` treats both the same.

**Inline — `product-view/index.tsx` (the `renderVariationAttribute?.(attr) ?? renderDefaultVariationAttribute(attr)` line):**
> This file picked up real branching logic in this PR but has never had its own test file, on develop or here. Per `testing.md`, a component with real prop-driven branching gets its own test even when the state it renders is proven elsewhere. The base template ships one for comparison — worth a small test asserting this override/fallback contract from this file's own folder.

Separately, worth knowing: `product-view/index.tsx` isn't actually in `protectedFiles.md`'s Tier 2 list at all, despite being shared across four consumers (PDP, quick-view modal, bonus-product modal) the same way `product-tile`/`swatch-group` are — that's a pre-existing gap in the doc, not something this PR touches, so I haven't drafted anything for it.

Want me to post this batch, or adjust anything first?

Yes — and it settles this more thoroughly than either of us guessed. That node is a dedicated "Out of stock / coming soon" spec page in the actual Designs file (separate from the design-system file I'd been checking), covering both the current-story design and a proposed enhancement.

In every single frame — current design and proposed enhancement, both "Coming soon" and "All items out of stock", both default and expanded states — the colour swatches render identically to a fully-available product: same two swatches, same bottom-border selected indicator, no dimming, no strikethrough. The stock signal lives entirely in two other places: the size selector switching to "Select size to be notified", and the CTA button changing style (solid grey in the current design, outlined in the proposed enhancement). The swatch itself never changes.

One honest caveat: this page shows whole-product unavailability (every size/colour gone), not the narrower case my original finding was about — one colour unavailable while its siblings are still fine. Figma doesn't show that exact scenario explicitly. But given the swatch stays untouched even when the *entire product* is dead, the same principle clearly extends to a single unavailable colour. So this isn't just "accepted as out of scope" anymore — it's confirmed as the correct behaviour per an explicit, deliberate design spec, not an omission.

That doesn't change anything in the comment batch — that item was already dropped per your last answer. Want me to go ahead and post it?
